title: Generative Actor-Critic with Soft Bridge Policies
claim: A single feedforward pass through stochastic bridge layers yields actions whose path-level KL to a reference process is analytically tractable.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right, shared base, KL markers between rows, summed energy bar
description: Two horizontal rows of small contour-plot panels show a 2D bridge. The top blue row is the actor bridge P_theta(tau|s). It starts at a K=0 logistic base panel on the left, then goes through K=1 to K=5, a K=6 endpoint, and a tanh step. The final panel is a multimodal endpoint distribution pi_theta(a|s). The bottom grey row is the reference bridge R(tau), with the same stages but ending in a noisy, near-uniform endpoint u_R(a). Blue arrows are labelled q_theta,k and grey arrows r_k. Orange dashed separators between the rows mark local KL terms. A long orange bracket underneath leads to the blue formula Control Energy C_theta(s,tau) = sum_k KL(q_theta,k || r_k). The eye goes first to the colorful panels and the endpoint contrast on the right.
caption: Overview of the proposed soft bridge policy. Local KL terms compare actor and reference transitions and sum to the sampled control energy. The terminal latent is mapped through tanh and optimized by the critic. Appendix C provides a 2D bridge visualization.
abstract: Expressive generative policies such as diffusion and flow models are appealing for maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) online reinforcement learning because of their ability to model multimodal and highly non-Gaussian action distributions. However, training effective soft generative policies faces two obstacles that often arise together. First, marginal action densities are often unavailable, so existing methods typically rely on entropy bounds, heuristic proxies or approximations. Second, iterative shared-parameter samplers raise inference cost and require backpropagation through time over repeated network evaluations, increasing memory cost and potentially destabilizing policy optimization. These obstacles motivate us to seek a generative actor-critic method that exposes a tractable soft objective while generating each action in just one network evaluation. To this end, we propose soft generative actor-critic (SoftGAC), whose actor is a single stochastic feedforward network with internal Gaussian bridge layers. This explicit bridge structure allows us to lift the soft objective to path space, yielding an analytical path-KL regularizer against a high-entropy reference process for both actor improvement and the soft Bellman bootstrap, without estimating the endpoint entropy. Crucially, the actor generates each action in only one network evaluation under a total parameter budget comparable to strong baselines, substantially reducing inference cost relative to the existing iterative diffusion and flow policies. It also avoids long unrolled backpropagation through time. Across challenging continuous-control benchmarks, our method achieves competitive or superior returns compared with strong diffusion and flow policies, demonstrating a clear advantage in the compute-return tradeoff.
